Overview

This project involves migrating the traceability static validation process from an existing Airflow DAG to a new Google Cloud Function. The new function will replicate the existing validation logic for CSV and Excel files, handle error reporting to GCS, update a database with the validation status, and trigger a downstream ingestion process upon success. This migration is intended to improve performance and maintainability of the validation step.
Affected repos:
traceability-service
Subtasks (7)
01 — Create Cloud Function Boilerplate and Scaffolding (traceability-service · small)

Create the basic scaffolding for the new Traceability Validation Cloud Function. This includes setting up the directory structure, a main entrypoint file, dependency management, and a basic deployment configuration.
Files
gcp/cloud_functions/traceability_validator/main.py
gcp/cloud_functions/traceability_validator/requirements.txt
Acceptance criteria
A new directory structure `gcp/cloud_functions/traceability_validator` is created.
A `main.py` file with a placeholder function signature is created.
A `requirements.txt` file is created containing `pandas` and `openpyxl`.
A basic deployment script or CI/CD configuration is in place to deploy the function.
02 — Implement File Reading for Excel and CSV (traceability-service · small)

Implement the logic to handle file I/O for the Cloud Function. The function will be triggered by a GCS event and must be able to read both Excel (.xlsx) and CSV (.csv) files from the GCS bucket into a pandas DataFrame for processing.
Files
gcp/cloud_functions/traceability_validator/main.py
gcp/cloud_functions/traceability_validator/file_handler.py
Acceptance criteria
The function correctly identifies the file type (CSV or XLSX) from the GCS event.
The function successfully reads a `.xlsx` file into a pandas DataFrame.
The function successfully reads a `.csv` file into a pandas DataFrame.
The file reading logic is encapsulated in a helper module.
03 — Port Static Validation Logic from DAG (traceability-service · medium)

Port the core validation logic from the existing Airflow DAG (`traceability_static_validations_checker.py`) to the new Cloud Function. This includes checks for mandatory columns and numeric data types. The logic should operate on the pandas DataFrame created in the previous step.
Files
gcp/cloud_functions/traceability_validator/validator.py
gcp/cloud_functions/traceability_validator/main.py
Acceptance criteria
Mandatory column checks from the original DAG are replicated.
Numeric column checks from the original DAG are replicated.
The function generates a list of validation errors in memory if any checks fail.
The function processes valid files without generating errors.
04 — Implement Error Report Generation and Upload (traceability-service · medium)

Implement the error reporting mechanism. If the validation fails, the function must generate a CSV report detailing the errors, name it according to the specified convention, and upload it to a designated GCS bucket.
Files
gcp/cloud_functions/traceability_validator/error_reporter.py
gcp/cloud_functions/traceability_validator/main.py
Acceptance criteria
On validation failure, a CSV error report is generated in the specified format (Row, Column, Reason).
The error report is uploaded to the correct GCS path.
The error report filename matches the pattern `{filename}_error_report_{timestamp}.csv`.
No error report is generated for successful validations.
05 — Implement Database Updates and Downstream Trigger (traceability-service · medium)

Integrate the Cloud Function with the database and the downstream Airflow DAG. The function needs to write the validation status (`staticValidationPassed` or `staticValidationFailed`) to a database and trigger the next step in the ingestion pipeline only upon success.
Files
gcp/cloud_functions/traceability_validator/main.py
gcp/cloud_functions/traceability_validator/integrations.py
Acceptance criteria
On success, the database is updated with a `staticValidationPassed` status.
On failure, the database is updated with a `staticValidationFailed` status and the GCS path to the error report.
The downstream ingestion DAG is triggered only on successful validation.
The downstream DAG is not triggered on validation failure.
06 — Develop Unit, Integration, and Performance Tests (traceability-service · large)

Develop a comprehensive suite of tests to ensure the new Cloud Function is reliable and meets all functional and performance criteria. This includes unit tests for the validation logic and integration tests for the end-to-end process.
Files
gcp/cloud_functions/traceability_validator/test_validator.py
gcp/cloud_functions/traceability_validator/test_integration.py
Acceptance criteria
Unit tests cover all validation logic for both CSV and Excel files.
Integration tests verify the complete workflow for a successful validation (file read, validation pass, DB update, downstream trigger).
Integration tests verify the complete workflow for a failed validation (file read, validation fail, error report upload, DB update, no downstream trigger).
Performance tests are created for 10MB, 100MB, and 250MB files.
07 — Decommission Old Airflow DAG (traceability-service · small)

Once the new Cloud Function has been deployed, tested, and verified in production, the old Airflow DAG and its associated configurations must be safely removed to prevent redundant executions and to complete the migration.
Files
airflow/dags/traceability_static_validations_checker.py
Acceptance criteria
The old Airflow DAG `traceability_static_validations_checker.py` is removed from the DAGs folder.
Any configurations related to the old DAG are removed.
A confirmation is received that no more instances of the old DAG are running or scheduled.
Risks (3)
The existing validation logic in `traceability_static_validations_checker.py` may have undocumented edge cases, making a perfect 1:1 replication challenging.
Meeting the performance criteria for large files (250MB) within the default Cloud Function environment may be difficult and could require significant memory allocation or code optimization.
The rollback plan requires careful monitoring post-deployment to quickly detect any validation gaps or performance regressions compared to the old DAG.
Open questions (3)
What is the specific mechanism for triggering the downstream ingestion DAG from the Cloud Function (e.g., Airflow API call, Pub/Sub message)?
What are the connection details and required permissions for the database that stores the validation status?
Where is the source code for the existing DAG `traceability_static_validations_checker.py` located?
